title: Catalog data quality and placement gates
caveat: Display/catalog integrity only. These cases do not measure recognition or recommendation quality.

cases.title: Schema and required fields
cases.spec: The manifest uses catalog-release-1 and every required field has the declared type.
cases.negativeExample: An item omits id or manifest.schema_version is unknown.

cases.title: Canonical identity and aliases
cases.spec: Canonical IDs and slugs are unique; aliases do not collide and resolve only to canonical items.
cases.negativeExample: Two items share a slug or an alias points to another alias.

cases.title: Display image roles
cases.spec: Every published item has a main image and thumbnail, card, and original roles allowed by display policy.
cases.negativeExample: A published item has no thumbnail role.

cases.title: Local complete references
cases.spec: All data and media references are relative, remain inside allowed roots, and name present manifest entries.
cases.negativeExample: A media path is absolute, traverses upward, or names a missing file.

cases.title: Exact bytes and decodable WebP
cases.spec: SHA-256 and byte length match exact bytes; media MIME is image/webp and fully decodes.
cases.negativeExample: A valid WebP header is followed by a truncated image body.

cases.title: Runtime image dimensions and roles
cases.spec: Decoded runtime bytes match declared dimensions; long-side role bounds and variant geometry relative to the master are valid. This does not prove that the upstream master was never cropped.
cases.negativeExample: A portrait thumbnail is 400x900, its declared dimensions differ, or a variant is larger than its master.

cases.title: Accepted display policy
cases.spec: Policy-hidden disputed values stay hidden; optional unknown fields are omitted rather than made into zero facts; source URLs are syntactically valid when present. Source truth is a separate preparation audit.
cases.negativeExample: A policy-suppressed category reappears or a source URL uses a non-HTTP scheme.

cases.title: Immutable complete manifest
cases.spec: Manifest entries exactly cover accepted runtime files; the release controller separately rejects catalog_version reuse with another manifest SHA.
cases.negativeExample: The controller registry already binds catalog_version to another SHA or a runtime file is unlisted.

cases.title: Target database projection
cases.spec: After import, target DB item/alias counts, IDs, active catalog version, and manifest SHA match the candidate.
cases.negativeExample: Dry-run passed but target DB still exposes the previous active version.

cases.title: Target HTTP media delivery
cases.spec: After deployment, catalog media returns exact accepted bytes with image/webp and immutable caching; internal files are unavailable.
cases.negativeExample: A card URL returns HTML, wrong bytes, or /internal/display-policy.json is public.

cases.title: Unexpected removed IDs
cases.spec: Every ID removed from the previous catalog is blocked unless the exact removed-ID set has explicit task approval and evidence reference. The authorized initial demo-to-real replacement set is the exact eight demo IDs.
cases.negativeExample: A newly added item masks one removed previous ID in aggregate counts.
